G5500:
* χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ (< χείρ, τείνω)
1. to vote by stretching out the hand in the Athenian ἐκκλησία (Luc., Plut.).
2. to appoint:
(a) by vote, 2 Corinthians 8:19
(b) without vote, Acts 14:23 (v. Rackham, in l.) (cf. προχειροτονέω).†

G5508: Χίος, -ου, ἡ Chios, an island in Ægean Sea: Acts 20:15.†

G5510: χιών, -όνος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג ;] snow: Matthew 28:3, Revelation 1:14.†
G5511: * χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ [in LXX: II Mac 12:35 * ;] a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (q.v.): Matthew 27:28, Matthew 27:31 (v. Tr., Syn., § 1).†

G5514: Χλόη, -ης, ἡ (i.e. tender foliage), Chloe: 1 Corinthians 1:11.†

G5517: χοϊκός, -ή, -όν, (< χοῦς) earthy, made of dust: 1 Corinthians 15:47-49 (v. Field, Notes, 179 f.).†

G5519: ** χοῖρος, -ου, ὁ [in Sm.: Isaiah 65:4 Isaiah 66:3 ;] a swine: pl., Matthew 7:6 Matthew 8:30-32, Mark 5:11-13, Mark 5:16, Luke 8:32-33 Luke 15:15-16 †
G5520:
** χολάω, -ῶ (< χολή), [in LXX: III Mac 3:1 R * ;]
1. to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.).
2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: c. dat. pers., John 7:23.†
G5521: χολή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה ;] gall: Matthew 27:34 (here prob. = myrrh, cf. Mark 15:23, v. Swete, in l.; DCG, i, 634a); metaph., Acts 8:23.†
G5522:
χοῦς, -οός acc., οῦν, ὁ, (contr. from χόος), [in LXX chiefly for עָפָר ;]
1. earth, soil.
2. In later writers (Plut., LXX), = κονιορτός, dust: Mark 6:11, Revelation 18:19.†
G5523: Χοραζείν (Rec. -ζίν), ἡ, Chorazin, a town of Galilee: Matthew 11:21, Luke 10:13.†
G5524:
χορηγέω, -ῶ (< χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;]
1. to lead a χορός (v. LS, s.v.).
2. to defray the cost of a χορός.
3. In late writers, metaph., c. acc. (v. M, Pr., 65), to supply, furnish abundantly: 2 Corinthians 9:10, 1 Peter 4:11 (Polyb., al.).†
G5525: χορός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מָחוֹל, מְחֹלָה ;] a dance: pl., Luke 15:26.†
G5527: † χόρτασμα, -τος, τό (< χορτάζω), [in LXX: Genesis 24:25, Genesis 24:32 Genesis 42:27 Genesis 43:24, Judges 19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), Deuteronomy 11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Si 30:33 (33:24)) Si 38:26 * ;] fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Acts 7:11 (RV, sustenance).†
G5528:
χόρτος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for עֶשֶׂב, also for חָצִיר, etc. ;]
1. an enclosure, a feeding place (Hom.).

(cl.), to treat, deal with, Acts 27:3.†
G5531: χράω, κίχρημι [in LXX for לוה, etc. ;] to lend: Luke 11:5.†
G5532:
χρεία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: 2 Chronicles 2:16 (צֹרֶךְ), Ezra 7:20 (חַשְׁחוּת) freq. in Si, I-II Mac ;]

G5533: † χρεοφειλέτης (Rec. χρεω-, WH, χρεοφιλ-; v. WH, App., 152, 154), -ου, ὁ, (< χρέος, a debt, + ὀφειλέτης) [in LXX: Job 31:37, Proverbs 29:13 * ;] a debtor: Luke 7:41 Luke 16:5.†
G5534: * χρή impers. (< χράω, v. LS, s.v.), it is necessary: James 3:10 (cf. δεῖ.).†
G5537:
χρηματίζω (< χρῆμα), [in LXX: Jeremiah 26:2 Jeremiah 29:23 Jeremiah 30:2 Jeremiah 36:2, Jeremiah 36:4 A (דּבר pi.), Jeremiah 25:30 (שׁאג), 1 Kings 18:27, Job 40:8 * ;]
1. to transact business, hence, to consult, deliberate (Thuc., Dem., al.); hence in later writers,
2. to make answer (esp. of offcial pronounce­ments by magistrates, etc.; in π. of the royal reply to an ἔντευξις, q.v.; cf. Deiss., BS, 122); of an answer by an oracle (Diod., Plut., al.); in FlJ, LXX and NT, of divine communications, to instruct, admonish, warn: pass. G5538: χρηματισμός, -οῦ), ὁ (< χρηματίζω, q.v.), [in LXX: Proverbs 31:1 (מַשָּׂא), II Mac 2:4 11:17 * ;] a divine response, an oracle: Romans 11:4 (Xen., Plat., al.).†
G5539: χρήσιμος, -η, -ον (< χράομαι), [in LXX: Genesis 37:26 בֶּצַע etc. ;] useful: 2 Timothy 2:14.†
G5540: χρῆσις, -εως, ἡ (< χράομαι), [in LXX: I Ki 1:28 (שׁאל), Si 18:8, al. ;] use: in a sexual sense, Romans 1:26; c. gen. obj., θηλείας, Romans 1:27 (for exx., v. Thayer, s.v.).†
G5541: *† χρηστεύομαι (< χρηστός), to be kind: 1 Corinthians 13:4 (eccl.).†
G5542: *† χρηστολογία, -ας, ἡ (χρηστός, λέγω), fair speaking: in bad sense, Romans 16:18 (in good sense also, eccl.).†
G5544:
χρηστότης, -ητος, ἡ (< χρηστός), [in LXX for מוֺב and cogn. forms ;]
1. goodness, excellence, uprightness: Romans 3:12 (LXX).
2. goodness of heart, kindness: Romans 2:4, 2 Corinthians 6:6, Galatians 5:22, Colossians 3:12, Titus 3:4; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Ephesians 2:7; id., opp. to ἀποτομία, Romans 11:22. SYN.: v.s. ἀγαθωσύνη.

Tdf., Pr., 102; Bl., § 4, 2), -τος, το (< χρίω), later form of χρῖμα (Æsch., al.), [in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms (Exodus 29:7, al.) ;] an anointing, unction (the result of the action χρίειν; ICC, in l.; but cf. χριστός (Χρ-), -ή, -όν (< χρίω), [in LXX for מָשִׁיחַ and cogn. forms ;]
1. as adj.,
(a) of things, anointing, to be used as ointment (Æsch., Eur., al.; τ. ἔλαιον τὸ χ., Leviticus 21:10);
(b) of persons, anointed (ὁ ἰερεὺς ὁ χ., Leviticus 4:5; οἱ χ. ἰευρεῖς, II Mac 1:10): ὁ χ. τοῦ κυρίου or Θεοῦ (I Ki 2:10, Psalms 2:2, al.), of the Messiah (Aram., מְשִׁיחָא; cf. Dalman, Words, 289 ff.), Luke 2:11, Luke 2:26 John 1:41, Acts 2:36 Acts 4:26, al.

G5559: χρώς, gen., χρωτός, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;] in cl. rare in prose, the surface of the body, skin: Acts 19:12.†

G5562:
χωρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Genesis 13:6 (נשׂא), 1 Kings 7:26, 1 Kings 7:38 (כּוּל hi.), 2 Chronicles 4:5 (חזק hi.), Wi 7:23, 24, al. ;]
I. Intrans.,
1. to make room, give way, retire, pass: seq. εἰς, Matthew 15:17; metaph. (EV, come), εἰς μετάνοιαν, 2 Peter 3:9.
2. to go forward, advance, progress (Plat., Polyb., al.) ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ. ἐν ὑμῖν, John 8:37 (R, txt., hath not free course; R, mg., hath no place, for wh. cf. Field, Notes, 94 f.).
II. Trans., to have space for holding, to hold: Mark 2:2 (cf. Genesis 13:6), John 21:25; of measures (1 Kings 7:26, 2 Chronicles 4:5), John 2:6. Metaph., of having or making room in mind or heart: Matthew 19:11-12 (EV, receive), 2 Corinthians 7:2 (R, txt., open your hearts; mg., make room) (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ὑπο-χωρέω).†

1. to separate, divide, put asunder: c. acc. rei, opp. to συζεύγνυμι Matthew 19:6, Mark 10:9; c. acc. pers., seq. ἀπό (Wi 1:3), Romans 8:35, Romans 8:39; pf. pass ptcp., Hebrews 7:26.
2. In late writers, mid. and 1 aor pass., to separate oneself, depart: Philemon 1:15; seq. ἀπό Acts 1:4, ἐκ, Acts 18:1-2; of divorce (polyb., al.), 1 Corinthians 7:10-11, 1 Corinthians 7:15 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-χωρίζω).†

(b) besides: Matthew 14:21 Matthew 15:38, 2 Corinthians 11:28.†
G5566: *† χῶρος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. corus), the N.W. wind: Acts 27:12.†
G5567:
ψάλλω [in LXX chiefly for זמר pi. (Judges 5:3, Psalms 7:17, al.), also for נגן pi. (1 Samuel 16:16, al.) ;]
1. to pull, twitch, twang (as a bowstring, etc.; Æsch., Eur., al.), hence,
2. absol.,
(a) to play a stringed instrument with the fingers (Hdt., Plat., al.);
(b) later, to sing to a harp, sing psalms (LXX); in NT, to sing a hymn, sing praise: James 5:13; c. dat. pers., Romans 15:9 (LXX), Ephesians 5:19; dat. instr., 1 Corinthians 14:15.†
G5568:
ψαλμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ψάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for מִזְמוֹר ;]
1. a striking, twitching with the fingers (Eur., al.), hence, a striking of musical strings (Æsch., al.), and hence in later writers,
2. a sacred song sung to musical accompaniment, a psalm (LXX): 1 Corinthians 14:26, Ephesians 5:19, Colossians 3:16; of OT psalms, Luke 24:44, Acts 13:33; βίβλος ψαλμῶν, Luke 20:42, Acts 1:20.† SYN.: v.s. ὕμνος
G5569: *† ψευδ-άδελφος, -ου, ὁ a false brother: of professing Christians, 2 Corinthians 11:26, Galatians 2:4.†
G5570: *† ψευδ-απόστολος, -ου, ὁ a false apostle: 2 Corinthians 11:13.†
G5571: ψευδής, -ές (< ψεύδομαι), [in LXX for שֶׁקֶר, שָׁוְא, כָּזָב; etc. ;] lying, false, untrue (of persons and things): Revelation 2:2; μάρτυρες, Acts 6:13; as subst., ὁ ψ., a liar: Revelation 21:8.†
G5572: † ψευδο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ a false teacher: 2 Peter 2:1.†
G5573: * ψευδο-λόγος, -ον (< ψευδής, λέγω), speaking falsely, lying: 1 Timothy 4:2 (Aristoph., Polyb., al.).†
G5574:
ψεύδω to deceive by lies; more freq. in the depon. mid, form ψεύδομαι (so always in NT), [in LXX chiefly for כּחשׁ pi. ;]
1. absol., to lie: Hebrews 6:18, 1 John 1:6, Revelation 3:9; οὐ ψεύδομαι, Romans 9:1, 2 Corinthians 11:31, Galatians 1:20, 1 Timothy 2:7 c. dat. pers. (Psalms 18:45, Jeremiah 5:12, al.), Acts 5:4; seq. εἰς, Colossians 3:9; κατά, James 3:14 (Hort, in l.).
2. Like act., c. acc., to deceive by lies (Æsch., al.): Acts 5:3.†
G5575: **† ψευδο-μάρτυς, -υρος, ὁ [in LXX: Da LXX Su 60, TH ib. 61 Bl * ;] a false witness: Matthew 26:60; c. gen. obj. (v. WM, § 30, 1a), 1 Corinthians 15:15.†
G5576: ψευδο-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Exodus 20:16, Deuteronomy 5:20 (ענה), Da TH Su61 AB2R (v. ψευδομάρτυς) * ;] to bear false witness: Matthew 19:18, Mark 10:19, Luke 18:20 (LXX); seq. κατά, c. gen. pers., Mark 14:56, Mark 14:57 (Xen., Plat., al.).†
G5577: * ψευδο-μαρτυρία, -ας, ἡ false witness: Matthew 15:19 Matthew 26:59.†
G5578: † ψευδο-προφήτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Zechariah 13:2, Je 9 (Jeremiah 6:13, al.) (נָבִיא)* ;] a false prophet (= cl. ψευδόμαντις): Matthew 7:15 Matthew 24:11, Matthew 24:24, Mark 13:22 (v. Swete, in l.), Luke 6:26, Acts 13:6, 2 Peter 2:1, 1 John 4:1, Revelation 16:13 Revelation 19:20 Revelation 20:10 †
G5579: ψεῦδος, -εος (-ους), τό [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶר, also for כַּחַשׁ, כָּזָב ;] a falsehood, untruth, lie: Revelation 14:15; opp. to ἡ ἀλήθεια, John 8:44, Romans 1:25, Ephesians 4:25, 2 Thessalonians 2:11, 1 John 2:21; to τὸ ἀληθές, 1 John 2:27; ποιεῖν ψ., Revelation 21:27 Revelation 22:15; ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει κ. σημείοις κ. τέρασιν ψεύδους (gen. qual., v. M, Th., 104; and on the meaning and construction, v. also ICC, in l.), 2 Thessalonians 2:9.†
G5580: *† ψευδό-χριστος, -ου ὁ a false Christ or Messiah, "a pretender to the Messianic office" (Swete, Mk., 309; cf. also Tr., Syn., § xxx): Matthew 24:24, Mark 13:22 (cf. ἀντίχριστος).†
G5581: * ψευδώνυμος, -ον (< ψευδής, ὄνομα) under a false name, falsely called: 1 Timothy 6:20 (Æsch., Plut., al.).†
G5582: ** ψεῦσμα, -τος, τό (< ψεύδω), [in Aq., Th.: Job 34:6, Proverbs 23:3; in Sm.: Job 13:4, al. ;] a lie, falsehood: Romans 3:7 (Plat., Plut. al.).†
G5583: ψεύστης, -ου, ὁ (< ψεύδω), [in LXX: Psalms 116:11 (כֹּזֵב), Proverbs 19:22 Aא2 (כָּזָב), Si 15:8 25:2 * ;] a liar: John 8:44, John 8:55, Romans 3:4, 1 Timothy 1:10, Titus 1:12, 1 John 1:10 1 John 2:4, 1 John 2:22 1 John 4:20 1 John 5:10 .†
G5584:
ψηλαφάω, -ῶ (< ψάω, to touch), [in LXX for מוּשׁ, משׁשׁ pi., etc. ;]
1. to feel or grope about; c. acc, to feel about for, search after: metaph., of seeking God, Acts 17:27.
2. to feel, touch, handle: c. acc. pers., Luke 24:39, 1 John 1:1; προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ (ὄρει ?), Hebrews 12:18 (R, txt., a mount that might be touched; mg., a palpable and kindled fire; v. Westc., in l.).†
G5585: ψηφίζω (< ψῆφος), [in LXX: 1 Kings 3:8 1 Kings 8:5 A (ספר ni..) * ;] to count (prop., with pebbles), reckon, calculate: τ. δαπάνην, Luke 14:28; τ. ἀριθμόν (i.e. calculate the number's meaning), Revelation 13:18 (in cl. chiefly mid., to vote by casting a pebble; cf. συγ-κατα-, συμ-φηφίζω).†
G5586:
ψῆφος, -ου, ἡ (< ψάω, to rub) [in LXX: Exodus 4:25 (צֹר), Lamentations 3:16 (חָצָץ), Ecclesiastes 7:26 (חֶשְׁבּוֺך), 2 Kings 12:4 A, Si 18:10, IV Mac 15:26 * ;]
1. a small smooth stone, a pebble: ψ. λευκή (for suggestions as to the meaning, v. Swete, in l.), Revelation 2:17.
2. From the use of pebbles in voting, a vote: Acts 26:10.†
G5588: * ψιθυριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (v. supr.), a whisperer (as epithet of Hermes, Dem., 1358, 6): in bad sense, Romans 1:30.† Syn.: καταλάλος, q.v
G5589: *† ψιχίον, -ου, τό dimin. of ψίξ, a crumb: Matthew 15:27, Mark 7:28.†
G5591: ** ψυχικός, -ή, -όν (< ψυχή) [in LXX: IV Mac 1:32 * ;] of the ψυχή (as the lower part of the immaterial in man), EV, natural: opp. to πνευματικός, 1 Corinthians 2:14 1 Corinthians 15:44, 1 Corinthians 15:46; πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες (EV, sensual; R, mg., natural or animal; better perhaps, of the mind; v. infr.), Jude 1:19; with ἐπίγειος, δαιμονιώδης, opp. to ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (σοψία), of the mind (Hort, in l.), James 3:15†
G5592: ψύχος (LT, ψῦ-, as in cl.), -εος (-ους), τό (< ψύχω), [in LXX: Genesis 8:22 (קֹר), Job 37:9, Psalms 147:17 (קָרָה), Zechariah 14:6, Da LXX TH 3:67,69 * ;] cold: John 18:18, Acts 28:2, 2 Corinthians 11:27.†
G5593: ψυχρός, -ά, -όν (< ψύχω), [in LXX: Proverbs 25:25 (קַר), Si 43:20, IV Mac 11:26 * ;] cold: sc. ὕδωρ (cf. Theogn., 263; Hdt., ii, 37), Matthew 10:42; metaph., of indifferent persons, Revelation 3:15, Revelation 3:16 †
G5594: ψύχω [in LXX for קוּר, שׁטח ;] to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaph., Matthew 24:12.†
G5595: ψωμίζω (< ψωμός, a morsel), [in LXX chiefly for אכל hi. ;] to feed with morsels (as children or the sick; Hippocr.), hence, generally, in late writers, to feed, nourish: c. acc. pers., Romans 12:20 (LXX); c. acc rei, to give out for food, 1 Corinthians 13:3 (cf. WM, § 32, 4an; for dupl. acc., cf. Numbers 11:4, Si 15:3, al.).†
G5596: † ψωμίον, -ου, τό dimin. of ψωμός, a fragment, morsel: John 13:26-27, John 13:30.†
G5597: † ψώχω (< ψώω, collat. form of ψάω, to rub) to rub: Luke 6:1.†
G5602:
ὧδε, adv., [in LXX for הֲֲלֹם ,פֹּה ,הִנֶּה, etc. ;]
1. prop., of manner, so (Hom., al.).
2. In poets (rarely) and late writers, of place,
(a) hither (Bl, §25, 2): Matthew 8:29, Mark 11:3, Luke 9:41, John 6:25, al.; ἕως ὧδε, Luke 23:5;
(b) here: Matthew 12:6, Mark 9:1, Luke 9:33, John 6:9, al.; τὰ ὧδε, Colossians 4:9; opp. to ἐκεῖ, Hebrews 7:8; ὧδε . . . ἢ ὧδε (ἐκεῖ), Matthew 24:23, Mark 13:21; metaph., here (i.e. in this circumstance or connection), 1 Corinthians 4:2, Revelation 13:10, Revelation 13:18 Revelation 14:12 Revelation 17:9.
G5604: ὠδίν (late form of ὠδίς), -ῖνος, ἡ [in LXX forחֶבֶל (and wrongly forחֶבֶל, cf. Ac, l.c.), חִיל, etc. ;] a birth pang, travail pain: 1 Thessalonians 5:3; metaph., of extreme suffering, Matthew 24:8, Mark 13:8; ὠδῖνες θανάτου (Psalms 18:4 הֶבְלֵימָוֶת), Acts 2:24.†
G5605: ὠδίνω [in LXX chiefly for חוּל, also for חבל pi., etc. ;] to have birthpangs, to travail: Galatians 4:27 (LXX), Revelation 12:2; metaph., Galatians 4:19 (cf. συν-ωδίνω).†
G5606: ὦμος, οὐ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for שְׁכֶם, כָּתֵף ;] the shoulder: Matthew 23:4, Luke 15:5.†
G5608: * ὠνέομαι, -οῦμαι to buy: ὠνήσατο (= cl. ἐπρίατο; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 210 ff.; Veitch, s.v.), c. gen. pret., Acts 7:16.†
G5610:
ὥρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for עֵת and in Da for שָׁעָה ;]
1. any time or period fixed by nature, esp. a season (Hom., Hdt., Plat., al.).
2. A part of the day, and esp. a twelfth part of day or night, an hour: Matthew 24:36, Mark 13:32, Acts 10:3, al.; accus. in ans. to "when"? (M, Pr., 63, 215; Bl., § 34, 8), John 4:52, Acts 10:3, Acts 10:30 1 Corinthians 15:30, Revelation 3:3; acc. of duration, Matthew 20:12 Matthew 26:40, Mark 14:37; inexactly, πρὸς ὥραν, for a season, for a time, John 5:35, 2 Corinthians 7:8, Galatians 2:5; πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας, for a short season (ICC, in l.), 1 Thessalonians 2:17.
3. A definite point of time, time, hour: Matthew 26:45; c. gen. rei, Luke 1:10 Luke 14:17, Revelation 3:10, al.; c. gen. pers., Luke 22:53, John 2:4 John 7:30, al.; ἡ ἄρτι ὥρα, 1 Corinthians 4:11; ἐσχάτη ὥ., 1 John 2:18; seq. ὅτε, John 4:21, John 4:23 John 5:25 John 16:25; ἵνα, John 12:23, al.; c. acc. et inf., Romans 13:11 (cf. DB, ext., 475b, 476b).
G5611: ὡραῖος, -α, -ον (< ὥρα), [in LXX for נָאָה, טוֹב, יָפֶה, etc. ;] seasonable, timely, esp. of ripe fruits; hence, blooming, beautiful (both of things and persons): Matthew 23:27, Acts 3:2, Acts 3:10, Romans 10:15 (LXX, ὥρα).†
G5612: ὠρύομαι depon., [in LXX for שׁאג ;] of animals (also of men, Hdt., al.), to roar, howl: λέων, 1 Peter 5:8.†
G5614: † ὡσαννά (T, ὠσ-) (Heb נָא and הוֹשֵׁעַ; v. Dalman, Words, 220 IL; Gr., 249), hosanna: Matthew 21:9, Mark 11:9-10, John 12:13; τ. υἱῷ Δανείδ, Matthew 21:9, Matthew 21:15.†
G5615: ὡσαύτως adv., strengthened for ὡς (in Hom, at the beginning of a clause, in the form ὣς δ' αὔτως, later in one word), in like manner, just so, likewise: Matthew 20:5 Matthew 21:30, Matthew 21:36 Matthew 25:17, Mark 14:31, Luke 13:5 Luke 20:31, Romans 8:26, 1 Timothy 5:25, Titus 2:6; with verb to be supplied from context, Mark 12:21, Luke 22:20, 1 Corinthians 11:25, 1 Timothy 2:9 1 Timothy 3:8 1 Timothy 3:11, Titus 2:3.†
G5617: Ὠσηέ (Tr., Ὁσ-), ὁ (Heb. הוֹשֵׁעַ), Hosea: Romans 9:25.†
G5618: ὥσ-περ adv., just as, even as: Matthew 6:2 Matthew 20:28, Acts 3:17, 1 Corinthians 8:5, 1 Thessalonians 5:3 al.; in protasis, with οὕτως (καί) in apodosis: Matthew 12:40, Luke 17:24, John 5:21, Romans 5:19, Galatians 4:29, James 2:26, al
G5619: * ὡσ-περ-εί adv., as, as it were: 1 Corinthians 15:8.†
G5620:
ὥσ-τε consecutive particle,
1. c. infin., expressing result, so as to: Matthew 8:24 Matthew 12:22, Mark 1:27, Luke 5:7, Acts 1:19, Romans 7:6, 1 Corinthians 1:7, Hebrews 13:6, al.; of a designed result, Matthew 10:1, Luke 4:29, al.; preceded by οὕτως, Acts 14:1; by τοσοῦτος, Matthew 15:33.
2. C. indic.,
(a) so that: Galatians 2:13, preceded by οὕτως, John 3:16;
(b) so then, therefore: Matthew 12:12, Mark 2:28, Romans 7:4, 1 Corinthians 3:7, Galatians 3:9, al.
3. so then, therefore: c. subjc., 1 Corinthians 5:8; c. imperat., 1 Corinthians 3:21 1 Corinthians 4:5, Philippians 2:12 1 Thessalonians 4:18, 1 Peter 4:19, al
G5621: *† ὠτάριον, -ου, τό = ὠτίον (q.v.), the ear: Mark 14:47, John 18:10.†
G5622:
ὠφέλεια (WH, -λία), -ας, ἡ [in LXX for יָעַל hi., בֶּצַע, etc. ;]
1. assistance, help (Thuc., Plat., al.).
2. profit, advantage, benefit (Hdt., Plat., al.): Romans 3:1, Jude 1:16.†
G5623: ὠφελέω, -ῶ (< ὄφελος), [in LXX chiefly for יָעַל hi. ;] to help, benefit, do good, profit: absol., Romans 2:25; οὐδέν (do no good; v. Field, Notes, 21), Matthew 27:24, John 6:63 John 12:19; c. acc pers., Hebrews 4:2; c. dupl. acc, Mark 8:36, 1 Corinthians 14:6, Galatians 5:2; pass., Hebrews 13:9; c. acc, Matthew 15:5 Matthew 16:26, Mark 5:26 Mark 7:11, Luke 9:25, 1 Corinthians 13:3.†
G5624: * ὠφέλιμος, -ον (< ὠφελέω), useful, serviceable, profitable: c. dat. commod., Titus 3:8; seq. πρός, c. acc, 1 Timothy 4:8, 2 Timothy 3:16.†
